mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% for 3 consecutive months prior to decision
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the previous 60-day period of lower rates (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when both PAYEMS growth and UNRATE decline are absent.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.3% suggests accelerating demand for goods and services, which elevates firm earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant correlation with CPIAUCSL momentum (Pearson's rho < 0.1, p < 0.01).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% indicates weakening supply-side conditions, which raises the risk of demand imbalances and tends to produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by > 2% in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during confirmed INDPRO contractions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 4%, it indicates a shift toward tighter policy, which reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 4%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive or flat despite the policy shift (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.5% and a rise in monthly pay growth (PAYEMS) above 0.5% indicates a robust labor market, which boosts investor sentiment and corporate valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% and PAYEMS > 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive when either UNRATE < 4.5% or PAYEMS > 0.5% alone (mutual exclusion test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) of more than 0.2% for three consecutive months suggests inflationary pressures are easing, which can reduce real interest rates and support equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during the CPIAUCSL deceleration (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) shows a double-digit decline in two consecutive months, it signals a deepening supply-side weakness that raises uncertainty and discourages investment, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by > 10% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant negative relationship with INDPRO declines (Pearson's rho > -0.2, p > 0.1).
